pairs.label: Gold / Silver (MCX)
pairs.why: The gold-silver ratio, the most watched precious-metals spread.

long_run.source: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly prices

pairs.label: Brent / WTI
pairs.why: The benchmark crude spread between the North Sea and US grades.

long_run.source: FRED daily spot prices, monthly averages

story.cause: Refinery outages in the US Midwest left crude piling up at Cushing, Oklahoma, WTI's delivery point, holding WTI below Brent.
story.ended: Back to normal within four months.
sources: US EIA, This Week in Petroleum, 2007

story.cause: A storage glut at Cushing during the 2008-09 crash pushed WTI below Brent.
story.ended: Back to normal within a month.
sources: US EIA, This Week in Petroleum, 2009

story.cause: Rising US shale and Canadian crude piled up at Cushing with too few pipelines to the Gulf Coast, while Libya's 2011 outage lifted Brent.
story.ended: New and reversed pipelines (Seaway in 2012) drained Cushing; the gap was back to normal in about two years, though WTI never regained its old premium to Brent.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, 2011-2013

story.cause: The pandemic crash, when storage filled and US crude briefly traded below zero.
story.ended: Back to normal within a month.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, Apr 2020

story.cause: The Strait of Hormuz closure from March 2026, and later the Iran conflict and tanker attacks, added a shipping-risk premium to seaborne Brent over inland WTI.
sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook, Oct 2026
Rigzone, Oct 2026: analysts look at the WTI-Brent spread

pairs.label: WTI / Natural gas
pairs.why: The oil-gas ratio: energy priced as liquid fuel against gas.

long_run.source: FRED daily spot prices, monthly averages

story.cause: Oil's run to $147 a barrel in July 2008 far outpaced gas.
story.ended: The crash brought the ratio back within months, just before the shale era began.
sources: US EIA, Short-Term Energy Outlook, 2008

story.cause: The shale gas boom: horizontal drilling and fracking flooded the US with gas, and Henry Hub fell below $2 in April 2012 while oil recovered to about $100.
story.ended: The ratio never went back to its pre-2009 range: a barrel of oil has bought far more gas ever since.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, 2012

story.cause: The pandemic oil crash; WTI went below zero on 20 April 2020.
story.ended: Back to normal within two months.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, Apr 2020

story.cause: Winter Storm Uri froze Texas gas production and spiked spot gas prices.
story.ended: Back to normal within a month.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, Feb 2021

story.cause: Europe's energy crisis pulled record US LNG exports and Henry Hub rose to about $9, its highest since 2008.
story.ended: Back to normal within five months as European demand eased.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, 2022

story.cause: Mild winters and record US gas output filled storage; Henry Hub fell below $2 in early 2024.
story.ended: Producers cut back and LNG demand grew; back to normal within nine months of the 2024 low.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, 2024

story.cause: Winter Storm Fern: Henry Hub spot hit a record $30.72 on 23 January 2026 and averaged $7.72 for the month.
story.ended: Back to normal within a month.
sources: US EIA, Today in Energy, Feb 2026 (https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=67046)

pairs.why: The copper-gold ratio, read as growth against safety.

long_run.source: IMF monthly prices (FRED) and World Bank Pink Sheet monthly prices
World Bank Pink Sheet monthly prices

pairs.label: Copper / Aluminium (MCX)
pairs.why: The two largest base metals, substitutes in wiring and cable.

story.cause: China's industrial boom lifted copper demand faster than mines could respond after years of low investment, while new Chinese smelters kept aluminium plentiful.
story.ended: The 2008 crash cut the ratio, but it never went back to its 1990s level: copper has stayed far dearer against aluminium since.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets / Commodity Markets Outlook, 2005-2008

story.cause: Copper set records on mine outages (the Grasberg mud rush of September 2025, with repairs expected to run to the end of 2027, and Kamoa-Kakula), US tariff plans that pulled metal into US warehouses, and demand from grids and data centers. Aluminium was tight too after the Strait of Hormuz closure curtailed Middle East smelters.
sources: S&P Global, Copper Market Report, Oct 2026
IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook, Jul 2026
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

pairs.label: Zinc / Lead (MCX)
pairs.why: Mined together and traded as a classic base-metal pair.

story.cause: A shortage of zinc ore: the fees smelters charge to process it fell below zero to record lows, while lead stayed well supplied. The World Bank expects zinc to ease from $3,500 a tonne in 2026 to $2,800 in 2028, with lead flat.
sources: Bloomberg, Jun 2026: China's zinc margins crushed as fees plunge to record lows
IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook, Jul 2026
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

story.cause: Zinc was in surplus with large exchange stocks while lead rallied on strong Chinese demand and tight supply.
story.ended: Zinc's 2005-06 rally brought the ratio back to normal within about a year.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2004-2005

story.cause: Zinc hit record highs as exchange stocks ran down and investors piled in.
story.ended: Zinc fell back as new mine supply arrived, and lead surged in 2007; the ratio was back to normal within months.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2007

story.cause: Lead hit a record in late 2007 after Australia's Magellan mine stopped shipping and China cut lead exports, while zinc slid.
story.ended: The ratio rose about a fifth within a year, but its 1990s level never returned: zinc and lead have traded closer together since.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2008

story.cause: Large zinc mines closed in 2015 (Century, Lisheen) and Glencore cut output, leaving a multi-year shortage of zinc ore and very low exchange stocks.
story.ended: New and restarted mines eased the shortage; each spike unwound within 4 to 18 months.
sources: World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, 2017-2019
International Lead and Zinc Study Group, 2017-2019

story.cause: Europe's energy crisis made power-hungry zinc smelting unprofitable, and smelters such as Nyrstar's Auby cut output.
story.ended: As power prices eased, so did the cuts; the ratio fell about 30% within a year.
sources: World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2022

story.cause: A shortage of zinc ore: the fees smelters charge to process it fell below zero to record lows, while lead stayed well supplied. The World Bank expects zinc to ease from $3,500 a tonne in 2026 to $2,800 in 2028, with lead flat.
sources: Bloomberg, Jun 2026: China's zinc margins crushed as fees plunge to record lows
IEA, Global Critical Minerals Outlook, Jul 2026
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

pairs.label: Copper / Zinc (MCX)
pairs.why: Construction and manufacturing demand on both legs.

story.cause: Copper stayed near records into mid-2008 while zinc had already fallen from its 2006 peak as new supply arrived.
story.ended: The financial crisis hit copper hard and the ratio fell about a quarter within a year, though not to its old level.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2009

story.cause: The zinc ore shortage after the 2015 mine closures lifted zinc against copper.
story.ended: The ratio returned to normal over two to three years as zinc supply recovered.
sources: World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, 2017-2019

story.cause: Copper's record run on mine outages, US tariff plans and demand from grids and data centers; zinc rose too on its own ore shortage.
sources: S&P Global, Copper Market Report, Oct 2026
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

pairs.label: Nickel / Copper (MCX)
pairs.why: Battery and steel demand against the broad industrial metal.

story.cause: Indonesia's fast-growing nickel smelting industry kept the market in surplus while copper rallied on its own shortages. Indonesia's 2026 cut to mining quotas lifted nickel only partly.
sources: Argus, 2026: Indonesia to cut nickel mining quota
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

story.cause: Booming stainless steel output, much of it in China, ran nickel stocks down.
story.ended: Nickel fell back within months.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2004

story.cause: Nickel hit a record above $50,000 a tonne in May 2007 on low exchange stocks and stainless steel demand.
story.ended: Chinese steelmakers switched to cheaper nickel pig iron and nickel halved within a year.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2008

story.cause: The financial crisis collapsed stainless steel demand, hitting nickel harder than copper.
story.ended: Back to normal within 6 to 13 months.
sources: World Bank, Global Commodity Markets, 2009

story.cause: Indonesia relaxed its ban on nickel ore exports in January 2017, adding to a surplus.
story.ended: Hopes for battery demand lifted nickel; the ratio rose about 40% within a year.
sources: World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, 2017-2018

story.cause: A short squeeze after Russia's invasion of Ukraine sent nickel above $100,000 a tonne intraday; the LME suspended nickel trading on 8 March 2022.
story.ended: Nickel fell back as Indonesian supply kept growing; the ratio was back to normal in about 18 months.
sources: LME, Mar 2022: nickel trading suspension
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Apr 2022

story.cause: Indonesia's fast-growing nickel smelting industry kept the market in surplus while copper rallied on its own shortages. Indonesia's 2026 cut to mining quotas lifted nickel only partly.
sources: Argus, 2026: Indonesia to cut nickel mining quota
World Bank, Commodity Markets Outlook, Oct 2026

relative_value.held_back: the cause looks lasting (Indonesia's fast-growing nickel smelting industry kept the market in surplus while copper rallied on its own shortages): past lasting extremes have not come back to normal
